The belief: keys are optional IDs. They help a widget test find something with
parameter in every public widget constructor, and otherwise they never change how a widget behaves.
Most of the time, that matches experience. A widget that's the only child of another widget generally doesn't need a key, as the
docs say, and static lists work fine without them. The half-truth is real: a key never changes what a widget looks like. What it changes is invisible until the list changes, and Flutter's own
makes the key a required argument for exactly that reason: without it, the item after a dismissed one would be synced with the dismissed item's state.
Elements are matched among siblings, in order
When a parent rebuilds, Flutter has to pair its new list of child widgets with its existing child elements. The
